title: Coherent driving of displacive Higgs fluctuations in superconductors
authors: Jacopo Fiore, Irene Zanotti, Kota Katsumi, N. P. Armitage, Claudio Castellani, Goetz Seibold, Lara Benfatto
abstract: Intense phase-stable terahertz (THz) laser pulses can drive collective modes coherently via multi-photon excitation pathways in a manner different than the standard resonant mechanism operative in linear response. Here we show that in superconductors the nonlinear optical response can be enhanced when excited quasiparticles activate a (non-resonant) static displacement of the superconducting order parameter, in full analogy with the displacive excitation of coherent phonons in opaque materials. By combining numerical simulations with analytical results we demonstrate that the displacive mechanism to excite the Higgs mode is operative in both $s$-wave and $d$-wave superconductors. We validate this prediction experimentally by the temperature dependence of the phase of the nonlinear first harmonic in superconducting $s$-wave NbN. We also discuss how the order-parameter relaxation at large times, which can be experimentally accessed via pump-probe protocols is connected to energy-dissipative processes. Our results offer a novel perspective on the ability of intense THz fields to measure, and eventually control, the parametric dependence of the optical response on collective degrees of freedom.
summary: This paper explores how intense THz laser pulses can coherently drive superconducting fluctuations via a mechanism analogous to phonon excitation, termed the displacive Higgs fluctuation. By calculating the nonlinear optical response, the authors demonstrate that this non-resonant coupling significantly enhances measurable signals near the superconducting gap edge in both s-wave and d-wave superconductors.
main_problem: Investigating the nonlinear optical response of superconductors driven by intense terahertz (THz) laser pulses, focusing on mechanisms beyond standard resonant linear response.
main_result: The displacive mechanism, involving a non-resonant static displacement of the superconducting order parameter, is shown to enhance the nonlinear first harmonic signal in both s-wave and d-wave superconductors.
method: Combining numerical simulations (using density matrix expansion) with analytical derivations based on diagrammatic methods to calculate nonlinear response functions.
model_or_system: Superconductors (s-wave and d-wave) modeled using a tight-binding Hamiltonian, incorporating disorder potentials. The analysis distinguishes between BCS quasiparticle contributions and bosonic collective modes like the Higgs mode.
key_observables: Nonlinear first harmonic current ($j_{NL}(\Omega)$), phase shift of the FH vs temperature, and time-domain signal decay rate ($\eta$).
important_parameters: THz pulse frequency ($\Omega$), superconducting gap magnitude ($\Delta$), disorder strength ($\gamma$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes a monochromatic pulse limit for simplicity; the treatment of disorder uses an 'exact configuration approach' in some parts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the enhancement of $j_{NL}(\Omega)$ at $\Omega=2\Delta$ when Higgs fluctuations are included (BCS+Higgs vs BCS), and compare theoretical predictions for static order-parameter fluctuations ($\delta\Delta(0)$) used in the nonlinear current formula.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need to study non-resonant response, developing the theoretical framework using density matrix expansions up to third order, demonstrating the mechanism via $j_{NL}(\Omega)$, and validating predictions through temperature dependence measurements (s-wave) or discussing limitations in unconventional pairing (d-wave).
why_interesting: The work directly bridges quantum optics/driven systems with many-body physics by using intense light fields to probe collective, non-equilibrium degrees of freedom (Higgs mode), which is highly relevant for understanding correlated materials dynamics.
